topic: A person's invention is already patented by someone else
text: I walked into the room, my heart light, carrying the sketches and blueprints of my invention—a device that could convert wind into usable energy, more efficiently than anything before. It was a breakthrough, a revolution, and it was mine. But as I laid the plans on the table, my colleague pointed to a thick envelope. Inside was a patent, identical to my design, filed just days before. The world felt a little smaller, the air a bit thinner. Yet, there it was, a testament of someone else's journey intersecting with my own. I must find a new path, a different angle, to shine the light of progress in another direction.
